slides.headline: He led the US government's global development agency. Now he leads a 110-year-old philanthropy. In 2026, TIME named him to its Philanthropy 100.
Dr. Rajiv J. Shah was named to the TIME100 Philanthropy 2026 list
slides.body: Shah is President of the Rockefeller Foundation - its 13th, and the first Indian-American to lead the institution since its founding over a century ago. TIME recognized his work directing the foundation's initiatives on global health, climate resilience, food security and economic opportunity.

slides.headline: He ran USAID - the US government's entire global development and humanitarian response agency.
slides.body: Born in Detroit to Gujarati immigrant parents, Shah served as the 16th Administrator of USAID from 2010 to 2015 before taking the Rockefeller Foundation presidency in 2017 - institutional leadership, not a single donation.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when its diaspora runs the institutions that set global development priorities, not just funds them.
slides.body: Shah's path from a government development agency to one of philanthropy's oldest institutions shows diaspora influence operating at the level of policy and strategy, not just individual gifts.
